passage.title: OUR COMMUNITY COOKING CLASS
passage.subtitle: Learning new recipes together
paragraphs: Every Tuesday evening, ten neighbours meet in the large kitchen of Oakwood Community Hall for a two-hour cooking class. Their teacher is Chef Marco, who worked in restaurants in Rome and Madrid for fifteen years before retiring.

Each week, the group learns how to make one simple, healthy dish from a different country. Last Tuesday, they cooked Spanish vegetable paella with saffron rice, peppers and peas. Next week, Marco wants to teach them how to make Japanese noodle soup.

Nobody needs to bring expensive knives or pans because the hall has got everything ready. Students only pay five pounds each week to cover the cost of fresh ingredients. Marco prints the recipe on a single sheet of paper so everyone can practise again at home.

At eight o'clock, after all the food is ready, everyone sits together around a long wooden table to eat dinner. Most members say the best part of the class isn't just learning to cook—it is chatting and laughing with their neighbours.
